title: Setting up your first employee: cover, pay, schedule and feedback
moduleTitle: Shared: Growing and managing a team
audience: Owners of small Australian property trade businesses who are about to take on their first employee
learningOutcomes: List the cover, registration and pay steps to complete before an employee's first working day.
Plan a weekly schedule that groups jobs by area to reduce travel time.
Set up a feedback routine that keeps the employee and the business improving.

instruction.heading: Cover before the first day
instruction.body: Before the first working day, confirm the workers compensation cover for the employee in the state or territory where the work is done. Confirm that the business's public liability cover applies when an employee works on client sites, and check the policy conditions on supervision and licensed work. Keep the policy number and the certificate in the business file.

instruction.heading: Pay and records
instruction.body: Register as an employer with the tax office and set up the payroll reporting the ATO requires. Pay the employee at least the minimum under the applicable award or agreement, and pay superannuation at the super guarantee rate. The ATO page checked on 2026-11-02 gives that rate as 12.00 per cent for 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027. Payroll software or a payroll service can help, but the owner remains responsible for the payments. Late pay is the quickest route to losing a worker and to starting a dispute.

instruction.heading: Scheduling for travel and skill
instruction.body: Plan the week so the employee and the owner are not spending the day in traffic. Group jobs by suburb or region, and keep a quieter day for the jobs further away. Work alongside the employee on the first few jobs, so that the owner can check the standard of work, how it is recorded and how the client is handled. Give each day a plan listing the job, the address, the scope, the materials, the access arrangements and the expected finish time. Record the start and finish time of each job, and its outcome. The schedule should also show when the owner will be on site, so that clients know who to expect.

instruction.heading: Feedback and handover
instruction.body: Hold a short feedback conversation each week for the first month, and a monthly one after that. Ask the employee what would make the work easier, what the business could do better and what they need. Write down the changes agreed, and check them at the next meeting. Plan for the possibility that a good employee will leave. Keep job records, standards and client details in the business systems rather than only in one person's head, so the work can pass to someone else without loss.

procedure: Confirm the workers compensation cover, and check the public liability policy for employee work.
Register for payroll, and confirm the reporting and withholding requirements with the ATO or an adviser.
Set pay at or above the applicable minimum, and set superannuation at the current rate.
Plan the week by grouping jobs by area, and reserve a slow day for distant work.
Work alongside the employee on the first few jobs, and record the standard of work and the client handling.
Book weekly feedback for the first month, and record the agreed changes.

workedExamples.situation: The owner plans two jobs for a new employee on the same day, one in the north of the city and one in the south. The owner has a third job in the middle.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How should the owner reschedule the day?
workedExamples.reasoning: The owner should group the two jobs by area, so that the employee and the owner travel the least. The distant job should move to a slow day, or the owner should work alongside the employee on the nearer jobs first. Cover and pay must be in place before the first day, whatever the schedule.

equipmentAndPpe: Daily job sheet with address, scope, access and expected finish time
Certificates of currency for workers compensation and public liability

commonErrors.error: Starting an employee before cover, payroll and pay terms are in place.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a start checklist, and do not roster the employee until each item is confirmed.

commonErrors.error: Scheduling jobs across the whole city on the same day.
commonErrors.prevention: Group jobs by area, and reserve a slow day for distant work.

commonErrors.error: Assuming feedback is unnecessary because the work looks fine.
commonErrors.prevention: Hold a short weekly feedback conversation for the first month, and record the actions agreed.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Workers compensation, payroll registration, withholding, superannuation timing and minimum pay are subject to Australian and state law. The super guarantee rate of 12.00 per cent for 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027 is confirmed from the ATO page checked on 2026-11-02.
An employee may do licensed work only if they hold the licence for it. Supervision does not replace a licence. This lesson grants no licence or permission.

qualityStandard: A start checklist shows cover, payroll registration, pay terms and superannuation as confirmed before the first day.
The weekly schedule groups jobs by area, and shows the owner's times on site.
Feedback actions are recorded, with an owner and a date.
documentationEvidence: Start checklist with cover certificates and payroll confirmation
Weekly schedule and daily job sheets with start and finish times
Feedback record with the agreed changes and review dates
summary: Cover, payroll and pay terms are in place before the first day.
Group jobs by area, and pair the first jobs with the owner.
Feedback and written records keep the business running if a person leaves.

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be in place before an employee's first working day?
options: Only a uniform and a name badge with a photo
Cover, payroll registration and confirmed pay terms
A social media account and a personal blog for the team
A completed business plan and a copy of the fleet map

knowledgeChecks.question: Which change reduces wasted travel time most?
options: Sending the employee to the job furthest from home each morning
Grouping jobs by area and reserving a slow day for distant work
Giving the employee the longest route each morning in the van
Keeping all jobs on one day of the week and the crew never works Mondays

knowledgeChecks.question: Why keep job records and standards in the business systems rather than in one person's head?
options: So the owner does not need to supervise and so the crew can work alone
So the work can be handed over without loss if a person leaves
So the employee can be paid less and the hours can be cut
So the client does not need an invoice and the quote is never sent
